papers.title: Lifespan EEG reference charts disentangle alpha-band alterations in neurological and neuropsychiatric disorders
papers.summary: Constructed lifespan reference charts for alpha peak frequency and power from raw and 1/f-adjusted EEG spectra in 22,094 outpatients and applied them to inpatients with mental disorders. Alpha power was uniformly reduced versus age-matched norms, but alpha peak frequency showed method-dependent dissociation: raw spectra suggested slowing while 1/f-adjusted estimates indicated acceleration.

papers.title: Lifespan EEG Reference Charts Reveal Aperiodic Confounds in Beta-Band Biomarkers Across Neurological and Neuropsychiatric Disorders
papers.summary: Built lifespan EEG reference charts for beta oscillations (N=22,094, ages 1-100) separating periodic from aperiodic activity and found beta power follows a tri-phasic lifespan trajectory and that aperiodic adjustment reverses the apparent developmental direction of beta frequency. Across seven disorders beta power was mostly reduced, but schizophrenia spectrum disorders showed reduced absolute yet increased aperiodic-adjusted beta power.

papers.title: Sleep electroencephalography-derived brain health and long-term cognitive decline in community-dwelling adults.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
papers.summary: Tested whether sleep EEG-derived Brain Health Score (BHS) and Brain Age Index (BAI) predict future cognitive decline in 639 Framingham Heart Study participants followed for an average of 14.3 years. Each 1-SD higher BHS was associated with slower decline in memory, executive function, and language, whereas BAI was not associated with change in any cognitive domain.

papers.title: Hyperventilation Unmasks Convergent Aperiodic EEG Vulnerability in Seizure Disorder and Schizophrenia
papers.summary: Created the first lifespan reference charts for hyperventilation EEG reactivity from 14,905 outpatient recordings, covering oscillatory and aperiodic parameters, and evaluated deviations in seizure disorder and schizophrenia. Both disorders showed divergent oscillatory signatures but converged on hyporeactive aperiodic offset with large effect sizes, suggesting a shared transdiagnostic marker of metabolic vulnerability.

papers.title: Diffusion MRI Tractography Predicts Electrophysiological Connectivity and Explains Spectral Signatures of Evoked Potentials in the Human Brain
papers.summary: Combining dMRI tractography and SEEG with single-pulse stimulation in 40 patients, the study found that structural connectivity predicts causal electrophysiological connectivity with high probability (~0.95 for presence, ~0.8 for absence). Direct pathways were marked by early phase-locked broadband activity (10-70 ms), while thalamic indirect pathways showed increased latency (>200 ms) and late oscillations.

papers.title: Stable Network Motifs with Divergent Engagement Across Memory Outcomes
papers.summary: Intracranial EEG in seven epilepsy patients during a visual recognition task showed that successful recognition is characterized by low modularity (Q=0.05), sustained cross-hemispheric integration of left MTL with right prefrontal cortex, and right-hemisphere dominance in directed connectivity (asymmetry index=0.33). Correct rejections instead showed early transient segregation and right-lateralized hubs.

papers.title: Adaptive Forgetting for Nonstationary Optimization: Towards Robust EEG Decoding
papers.summary: Proposed AFOR, a tensor-wise adaptive optimizer that replaces Adam's fixed second-moment decay coefficient with an online dynamic coefficient estimated from local gradient state for cross-subject EEG decoding. Under a strict cross-subject protocol on three EEG benchmarks, AFOR achieved the best average performance and improved mean test accuracy over Adam by 3.00%, 2.07%, and 4.38%.

papers.title: Infants at high and low likelihood for autism show different EEG developmental trajectories in speech tracking and statistical learning.
papers.summary: Longitudinal high-density EEG in 44 infants at high and low likelihood for autism revealed reduced syllable-level neural tracking in high-likelihood infants, correlating with verbal outcomes. High-likelihood infants also showed reduced novelty orientation during word recognition, while multi-talker variability disrupted segmentation in low-likelihood infants but not high-likelihood infants.

papers.title: Effects of Optic Flow on Electrocortical Dynamics During Walking and Stepping Over Virtual Obstacles.
papers.summary: Using a treadmill-based virtual reality paradigm with EEG, this study found that optic flow during obstacle avoidance enhanced pre-obstacle alpha desynchronization and induced sustained occipital theta synchronization, indicating distinct neural signatures for visual motion processing and motor planning.

papers.title: Explainable machine learning for Alzheimer's disease characterization using small-sample EEG data.
papers.summary: This study evaluated an interpretable resting-state EEG framework using spectral and nonlinear complexity features from 63 participants (36 AD, 27 HC). Ridge Logistic regression achieved an exploratory AUC of 0.912 and accuracy of 0.857 under leave-one-subject-out cross-validation; SHAP analysis highlighted posterior alpha activity, frontal and temporal theta power, and theta/alpha ratio, while microstate analysis revealed reduced Class B occurrence and increased Class C/D duration in AD.

papers.title: Electroencephalography as a biomarker of brain function in domestic ruminants: a systematic review and critical appraisal.
papers.summary: This systematic review evaluated EEG as a biomarker of brain function in domestic ruminants, synthesizing 112 studies across consciousness, nociception, anesthesia, hypoxia-ischemia, neurodevelopment, and neurological disorders. The review found that EEG consistently reflects context-dependent cortical activity but interpretation is limited by methodological heterogeneity; it recommends standardization and integration with complementary physiological measures.

papers.title: Validation of Low-Frequency Oscillatory Activity as an Indicator of Post-Stroke Injury and Recovery.
papers.summary: This study validated delta (1-3 Hz) and beta (20-30 Hz) EEG oscillatory activity as markers of post-stroke injury and recovery in an independent cohort of 30 individuals with stroke and 17 controls. Elevated delta coherence between bilateral motor cortices at admission decreased over time, paralleling motor recovery, and greater corticospinal tract injury and lesion volume were associated with greater delta and beta coherence and delta power.

papers.title: BH-CMA: A cross-modal attention network based on brain-heart collaboration for stress cognitive state decoding.
papers.summary: The study proposed BH-CMA, a cross-modal attention network for decoding four stress cognitive states using EEG and heart rate variability from 28 participants. Under leave-one-subject-out evaluation, BH-CMA achieved 58.07% accuracy, 55.54% Macro F1, and 81.74% Macro AUC, improving Macro F1 by 4.15% over EEG alone and showing that masking HRV reduced performance in 21 participants.

papers.title: Reduced information sharing within the orienting network predicts intelligence in late childhood.
papers.summary: This study examined 38 children aged 11–14 performing the Attention Network Test with EEG to link attentional network efficiency to intelligence. Reduced nonlinear information sharing (weighted Symbolic Mutual Information) within the orienting network predicted higher Full-Scale IQ, while local ERP and frontal midline theta measures showed no reliable associations.

papers.title: Electroencephalography Monitoring for Seizure Risk Stratification in the Critically III.
papers.summary: This review outlines the role of continuous EEG for diagnosing electrographic seizures and epileptiform abnormalities in critically ill patients and describes risk-stratification approaches, including the validated 2HELPS2B score, to optimize monitoring duration and resource use. It emphasizes that many ICU seizures are clinically silent and that risk-guided cEEG can improve efficiency in critical care.

papers.title: Pre-stimulus alpha power during mind-wandering in adults with ADHD.
papers.summary: EEG was recorded during a Go/No-Go task with thought probes in 28 medication-naïve adults with ADHD and 28 controls to characterize pre-stimulus alpha power dynamics during mind-wandering. Controls showed higher global alpha power without increased variability during mind-wandering, whereas ADHD patients exhibited no alpha power modulation between attentional states and higher alpha power variability during mind-wandering.

papers.title: EEG functional connectivity measures for differentiating 6-month consciousness-related outcome after brain injury.
papers.summary: In 111 patients with impaired consciousness after brain injury, the study explored whether EEG functional connectivity measures (wPLI, wPLI2, coherence) are associated with 6-month command-following outcome. Alpha-band wPLI during a moving condition showed a nominal group difference (p=0.006) but did not survive FDR correction (pFDR=0.169) and did not significantly improve discrimination beyond age and GCS (AUC 0.733 vs. 0.778 for clinical variables alone).

papers.title: Auditory stimuli extend the temporal window of visual integration by modulating alpha-band oscillations
papers.summary: EEG and tACS experiments showed that a brief auditory stimulus widens the temporal integration window for successive visual flashes by transiently reducing poststimulus instantaneous alpha frequency, with individual alpha-cycle lengthening correlating with fusion threshold prolongation, and a phase-resetting model reproduced the findings.

papers.title: Quantitative assessment of heart-brain coupling in neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy.
papers.summary: This pilot study assessed neuro-cardiac coupling using synchronized long-term EEG and ECG in 61 neonates with hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE). Neuro-cardiac synchronization (aEEG envelope and HRV) was significantly reduced in patients with abnormal EEG backgrounds compared to those with continuous normal voltage (median Spearman's r = 0.09 vs. 0.22, p = 0.015), and machine learning models achieved up to 90.22% accuracy for HIE grading using combined ECG features.

papers.title: N,N-Dimethyltryptamine and harmine formulation alters transient EEG topography sequences near the peak of the psychedelic state.
papers.summary: In a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled EEG study with 25 participants, the effects of an ayahuasca-inspired DMT/harmine formulation on EEG microstate dynamics were compared to harmine alone and placebo. DMT/harmine was associated with reduced microstate duration, increased occurrence and complexity, and less random transition sequences, consistent with increased metastability and signal diversity.

papers.title: A cell type-specific switch in GluN2D NMDA receptors drives cortical circuit hyperexcitability and sensory-driven cortical synchronization deficits in a Fragile X Syndrome model.
papers.summary: Using pharmacology and cell type-specific genetic manipulation in Fmr1 KO mice, this study tested the role of GluN2D-containing NMDA receptors in cortical circuit dysfunction in Fragile X Syndrome. Pharmacological inhibition of GluN2D corrected cortical hyperexcitability, reduced sensory-driven seizures, and improved EEG synchrony, revealing a cell type-specific switch in GluN2D expression from inhibitory to excitatory neurons.

papers.title: Machine Learning Using Electroencephalography Predicts Acute Cerebral Injury in the Pediatric ICU.
papers.summary: This prospective study applied multiple machine learning classifiers to clinical and EEG background features to predict acute cerebral injury in 201 pediatric ICU patients. The support vector machine with radial basis function kernel achieved the highest accuracy for binary injury detection (AUROC 0.95, test accuracy 0.90), while logistic regression performed best for multiclass unilateral versus bilateral injury classification (test accuracy 0.77).

papers.title: Electroencephalography-functional magnetic resonance imaging using a familial temporal lobe epilepsy model in cats: an exploratory methodological pilot study.
papers.summary: This exploratory methodological pilot study implemented simultaneous EEG-fMRI in cats with familial spontaneous epilepsy and identified amygdalo-hippocampal BOLD activation in 16/30 sessions using small-volume correction, but individual-level epileptogenic zone localization remained insufficient for clinical use.

papers.title: Preparation of Acute Mouse Hippocampal Brain Sections for Transport to a Distant Electrophysiology Laboratory.
papers.summary: The paper describes a standardized protocol for preparing and transporting acute mouse hippocampal slices to distant electrophysiology laboratories, emphasizing viability preservation during transport via sucrose-based protective solutions, controlled rewarming, and oxygenated aCSF in sealed containers. Validation with patch-clamp recordings showed that electrophysiological properties, including resting membrane potential, input resistance, action potential firing, and spontaneous synaptic neurotransmission, remained comparable to freshly prepared slices.

papers.title: Age-related cortical mechanisms underlying postural control: a systematic review.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 37 studies (1,302 participants) characterized age-related alterations in cortical activity during standing balance tasks with sensory, cognitive, and mechanical challenges. The evidence indicated that older adults show diminished task-dependent cortical modulation, weaker associations between cortical activity and postural sway, and delayed sensorimotor processing during challenging balance tasks compared to younger adults.

papers.title: Quantum machine learning for detection of sleep deprivation from EEG signals
papers.summary: This study applied Quantum Support Vector Machine and Hybrid Quantum Neural Networks to classify sleep-deprived versus well-rested states using resting-state EEG features, including spectral band power, band ratios, Hjorth parameters, and functional connectivity. The Hybrid Quantum Neural Network achieved the highest performance with 96.88% accuracy at the epoch level and 81.25% at the subject level, outperforming previously reported results.

papers.title: Resting-state EEG biomarkers of general and domain-specific cognitive impairment and plasma P-tau217 in patients with Alzheimer's disease and mild cognitive impairment.
papers.summary: This study examined resting-state quantitative EEG biomarkers in 360 participants (AD dementia, MCI, and healthy controls) for detecting cognitive impairment and associations with plasma P-tau217. EEG achieved AUCs of 0.70–0.87 for distinguishing AD-related cognitive dysfunction, and right parietal relative power was negatively correlated with and an independent factor for increased plasma P-tau217 (AUC 0.68).

papers.title: EEG reveals what the eyes can't see: A clinical vignette of epileptic visual loss.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.summary: A clinical vignette describes a case of epileptic visual loss in which EEG revealed seizures despite the patient's inability to see. The case highlights the diagnostic role of EEG in identifying occult ictal activity underlying visual loss.

papers.title: Millifluidic triMEA organoid platform with stretchable microelectrode arrays for parallel organoid electrophysiology under standardized perfusion.
papers.summary: The paper presents a triMEA millifluidic platform integrating three stretchable microelectrode arrays in one device to provide uniform perfusion across three independent wells, enabling simultaneous electrophysiological recordings from three human midbrain organoids. Computational and experimental validation confirmed stable fluidic profiles and successful parallel recordings under continuous perfusion.

papers.title: EEG Microstate Alterations in Anhedonia Subtypes of Major Depressive Disorder and Their Modulation by Intermittent Theta-Burst Stimulation.
papers.summary: The study stratified 50 MDD patients into high- and low-anhedonia groups and assessed EEG microstate dynamics before and after 2 weeks of intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS). High-anhedonia patients showed persistent microstate abnormalities after iTBS, while low-anhedonia patients largely normalized, suggesting subtype-specific neuromodulation effects and a potential treatment response marker.

papers.title: Antiseizure medication use during hospitalization and at discharge in critically Ill children undergoing continuous EEG monitoring.
papers.summary: This prospective cohort of 705 critically ill children undergoing continuous EEG characterized antiseizure medication (ASM) use and found that 54% received ASM, with electrographic seizures/status epilepticus strongly associated with inpatient ASM use (OR 19.73) and discharge prescribing (OR 4.79). Notably, ASM was frequently continued beyond documented seizures, and levetiracetam was the predominant first-administered non-benzodiazepine ASM.

papers.title: Multimodal neuroimaging in schizophrenia: a systematic review of EEG and fMRI integration.
papers.summary: A systematic review of 16 simultaneous EEG-fMRI studies in schizophrenia found consistent evidence of impaired sensory gating (abnormal P50 suppression, reduced P300), dysregulated gamma/beta oscillations, and default mode network alterations. The authors highlight altered fMRI responses to EEG events, suggesting possible neurovascular decoupling, but note methodological heterogeneity limits conclusions.

papers.title: Reversible visual pareidolia and ictal bradykinesia associated with a left parieto-occipital cavernous malformation: illustrative case.
papers.summary: A 36-year-old male with drug-resistant epilepsy presented with visual pareidolia (perceiving plastic bags as cats) and ictal bradykinesia due to a left parieto-occipital cavernous malformation. Microsurgical resection resolved both symptoms completely, but postoperative EEG showed persistent left frontotemporal sharp waves, indicating a secondary epileptogenic network.

papers.title: High-Density Spectral Analysis for Bi-Atrial Arrhythmogenic Substrate During Non-Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation.
papers.summary: High-density CARTOFINDER mapping in 47 non-paroxysmal AF patients showed that both focal and rotational activation sites exhibited higher dominant frequency deviation (DFD) and regularity index (RI) than non-focal/non-rotational sites, with the left atrium demonstrating higher DFD and RI than the right atrium. High-repetition rotational sites had higher RI but paradoxically lower DFD compared to low-repetition sites.

papers.title: Delayed late ventricular depolarization is associated with inflammation in epicardial Fat Among females: a New avenue in cardiac electrophysiology.
papers.summary: In 146 cardiac surgery patients, epicardial adipose tissue inflammatory and fibrotic markers correlated with delayed late anteroseptal depolarization (prolonged S-wave upstroke time) in females but not males, with linear regression confirming sex-specific associations for CD14, CD16, DEFA3, and COL1A2. Findings suggest that ECG can indicate adverse epicardial adipose tissue phenotypes in a sex-dependent manner.

papers.title: Effectiveness and multidimensional mechanisms of close-to-bone needling in knee osteoarthritis: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: Randomized controlled trial in 70 knee osteoarthritis patients found that close-to-bone needling (CBN) produced greater improvements in WOMAC, ISOA, and SF-36 scores, greater reductions in cartilage degeneration, synovial thickening, and joint effusion, and stronger modulation of miR-140, miR-30, IL-1β, and TNF-α compared to celecoxib. EEG analysis revealed reduced Delta/Theta power, increased Alpha/Beta/Gamma power in frontoparietal regions, and normalization of prefrontal connectivity in CBN group.

papers.title: Pediatric MOGAD in the Intensive Care Unit: A Case Series.
papers.summary: Retrospective review of 124 pediatric MOGAD patients identified 37 requiring ICU admission for altered mental status, seizures, or weakness; 16 were intubated, 18 had seizures, and 12 had neuroimaging evidence of increased intracranial pressure. The study characterizes severe MOGAD presentations but found no specific EEG biomarkers for MOGAD.

papers.title: Glycerol Phenylbutyrate Treatment in a Pediatric Cohort of SLC6A1-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder.
papers.summary: Retrospective review of 14 pediatric SLC6A1-NDD patients in Spain found that among 11 treated with glycerol phenylbutyrate, 80% of those with uncontrolled seizures at baseline had significant seizure reduction and 40% became seizure-free; 64% showed improved video-EEG abnormalities, with less improvement in cognitive and psychiatric manifestations. Side effects occurred in 7 of 11 treated patients, leading to discontinuation in 3.

papers.title: Modulation of immune responses by acupuncture at Jing-Well points in neurological disorders: exploring mechanisms and clinical applications in the era of modern electrophysiology.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on acupuncture at Jing-Well points for modulating immune responses in neurological disorders, focusing on neuroimmune, electrophysiological, and clinical aspects. It reports that direct evidence for Jing-Well point stimulation is limited, but broader acupuncture research suggests anti-inflammatory, autonomic, and neuroprotective effects, highlighting the need for standardized studies.

papers.title: Non-muscle proteins alleviate 118 °C sterilization-induced gel quality deterioration by non-covalently modulating myofibrillar protein conformation and aggregation.
papers.summary: The study compared soy protein isolate (SPI), egg white protein (EWP), and whey protein concentrate (WPC) for alleviating quality deterioration of surimi gels sterilized at 118°C. Supplementation with 4% SPI was most effective, increasing gel strength by 49.15% and water holding capacity by 7.6%, by promoting myofibrillar protein unfolding and cross-linking while inhibiting excessive aggregation.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
